data.title: Which article follows the accusative preposition?
data.description: One question per preposition — a random 10 each time.
learningPoints: durch, für, gegen, ohne, um always take the accusative — only der → den changes.

sections.explain: der Park is masculine; durch takes the accusative, so der → den.
die Stadt is feminine; feminine stays die in the accusative.
das Fenster is neuter; neuter stays das in the accusative.
Plural takes die in the accusative.
der Test is masculine; für takes the accusative (der → den).
die Frau is feminine; feminine stays die.
das Kind is neuter; neuter stays das.
Plural takes die.
der Plan is masculine; gegen takes the accusative (der → den).
die Idee is feminine; feminine stays die.
das Feuer is neuter; neuter stays das.
Plural takes die.
der Schlüssel is masculine; ohne takes the accusative (der → den).
sections.sentence: Ohne _ Schlüssel komme ich nicht rein.

sections.explain: die Jacke is feminine; feminine stays die.
das Handy is neuter; neuter stays das.
sections.sentence: Ohne _ Handy geht er nicht aus.

sections.explain: Plural takes die.
der Tisch is masculine; um takes the accusative (der → den).
die Ecke is feminine; feminine stays die.
das Haus is neuter; neuter stays das.
Plural takes die.

data.title: Which article follows the dative preposition?
data.description: One question per preposition — a random 10 each time.
learningPoints: aus, außer, bei, gegenüber, mit, nach, seit, von, zu always take the dative.

sections.explain: der Wald is masculine; aus takes the dative (der → dem).
die Schweiz is feminine; feminine dative is der.
das Regal is neuter; neuter dative is dem.
sections.sentence: Er nimmt das Buch aus _ Regal.

sections.explain: Plural dative is den (and the noun adds -n).
der Lehrer is masculine; außer takes the dative (der → dem).
die Chefin is feminine; feminine dative is der.
das Baby is neuter; neuter dative is dem.
Plural dative is den (+ -n on the noun).
die Familie is feminine; feminine dative is der.
das Wetter is neuter; neuter dative is dem.
sections.sentence: Bei _ Wetter bleibe ich zu Hause.

sections.explain: Plural dative is den (+ -n on the noun).
der Bahnhof is masculine; gegenüber takes the dative (der → dem).
die Schule is feminine; feminine dative is der.
das Museum is neuter; neuter dative is dem.
Plural dative is den (+ -n on the noun).
der Bus is masculine; mit takes the dative (der → dem).
die Hand is feminine; feminine dative is der.
das Auto is neuter; neuter dative is dem.
Plural dative is den (+ -n on the noun).
der Film is masculine; nach takes the dative (der → dem).
die Schule is feminine; feminine dative is der.
sections.sentence: Nach _ Schule gehe ich nach Hause.

sections.explain: das Essen is neuter; neuter dative is dem.
der Unfall is masculine; seit takes the dative (der → dem).
sections.sentence: Seit _ Unfall geht es ihm besser.

sections.explain: die Prüfung is feminine; feminine dative is der.
das Unglück is neuter; neuter dative is dem.
die Arbeit is feminine; von takes the dative (die → der).
Plural dative is den (+ -n on the noun).
sections.sentence: Das ist das Auto von _ Nachbarn.

sections.explain: Plural dative is den (+ -n on the noun).

data.title: Movement or location? Choose the right article.
data.description: One question per preposition — a random 10 each time.
learningPoints: Two-way prepositions: accusative for movement (wohin?), dative for location (wo?).

sections.explain: Movement (wohin?) → accusative; die Wand stays die.
sections.sentence: Ich hänge das Bild an _ Wand.

sections.explain: Location (wo?) → dative; feminine die → der.
Movement (wohin?) → accusative; der Tisch → den.
sections.sentence: Ich lege das Buch auf _ Tisch.

sections.explain: Location (wo?) → dative; der Tisch → dem.
Movement (wohin?) → accusative; das Haus stays das.
Location (wo?) → dative; das Haus → dem.
Movement (wohin?) → accusative; die Schule stays die.
Location (wo?) → dative; die Schule → der.
Movement (wohin?) → accusative; die Tür stays die.
Location (wo?) → dative; die Tür → der.
Movement (wohin?) → accusative; der Tisch → den.
sections.sentence: Ich hänge die Lampe über _ Tisch.

sections.explain: Location (wo?) → dative; der Tisch → dem.
Movement (wohin?) → accusative; der Tisch → den.
Location (wo?) → dative; der Tisch → dem.
Movement (wohin?) → accusative; die Tür stays die.
sections.sentence: Ich stelle das Auto vor _ Tür.

sections.explain: Location (wo?) → dative; die Tür → der.
Movement (wohin?) → accusative; plural stays die.
sections.sentence: Ich stelle den Stuhl zwischen _ Tische.

sections.explain: Location (wo?) → dative; plural die → den (+ -n).

data.title: Which contraction fits?
data.description: One question per preposition — a random 10 each time.
learningPoints: Preposition + article merge: an dem → am, in das → ins, zu der → zur …

sections.explain: gehen = movement → zu dem = zum.
sind = location → in dem = im.
fahren zu + feminine Arbeit → zu der = zur.
springen = movement into → in das = ins.
Days take an dem = am.
movement to the sea → an das = ans.
sein = location → bei dem = beim.
coming from → von dem = vom.
Seasons take in dem = im.
laufen = movement → zu dem = zum.
denken an + accusative → an das = ans.
'while eating' = location → bei dem = beim.

data.title: For things: da- (statement) or wo- (question)?
data.description: One question per preposition — a random 10 each time.
learningPoints: For things, attach da-/wo- to the preposition instead of a pronoun.

sections.explain: einverstanden MIT → da + mit = damit.
helfen MIT → wo + mit = womit.
sparen FÜR → da + für = dafür.
brauchen FÜR → wo + für = wofür.
denken AN → da + (r)an = daran.
denken AN → wo + (r)an = woran.
sich freuen ÜBER → da + (r)über = darüber.
sprechen ÜBER → wo + (r)über = worüber.

data.title: wo? · wann? · wohin? — choose the right word.
data.description: One question per preposition — a random 10 each time.
learningPoints: The same preposition can answer where, when, or where to.

sections.explain: Location (wo?) → dative; die Stadt → der.
Location (wo?) → dative; der Tisch → dem.
Location (wo?) → dative; die Ecke → der.
Days take am.
Clock times take um.
Seasons take im.
Movement (wohin?) → accusative; die Stadt stays die.
gehen zu + feminine Schule → zur.
